rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 is the best raced design (138.6). It has five 16 mm sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=-0.05 to +0.05 m, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 4.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.6 and base_speed 1.0. Its oval has 1 finish in 20 and s-bend progress is 0.295. Remaining faults are max error at about 0.062 m (just past the 0.06 m limit), 1.25 line-loss events per s-bend run, and oval steering oscillation of 0.30.

Iteration 7 widened the span to +/-0.07 m and raised kp to 5.0. That scored 96.0: oval progress fell from 0.55 to 0.39, slalom line losses rose from 1.0 to 1.95, and no run finished. Widening the sensor spacing with unchanged weights lowers the steering signal per centimetre, so the wider layout did not help. I therefore return to the iteration 6 geometry, which is the proven base.

Changes on the controller only: kp raised from 4.0 to 4.5 to restore some correction strength at the bends, and kd raised from 0.6 to 0.8 to damp the overshoot that shows up as oscillation and max error. ki 0.5 and base_speed 1.0 are kept, since they produced the only oval finishes.

Expected result: max error near or below 0.06 m, fewer line-loss events on the s-bend, and oval completions at or above the iteration 6 rate. Completion on the s-bend or slalom is still unlikely in this round.
